title: Continual output gaps and queue starvation fixes
creator: Nora Kaplan
description: Summary: During a capacity spike on 2026-03-03 several hosted API sessions experienced intermittent output gaps: clients received partial token runs followed by silent pauses and ultimately socket disconnects after three minutes. A subset of requests were starved by an internal priority queue where short-lived prefix requests blocked continuous streaming lanes. This ticket captures the investigation, immediate mitigations applied during the incident, and the tracked action items to prevent recurrence.
root_cause_summary: A regression introduced a queue prioritization change in the scheduler (commit gh:open/infra#b2f3c) that caused non-streaming control requests to preempt streaming flows under CPU-constrained scheduling windows. Combined with an aggressive per-session token flush policy and a KV-cache eviction race, streaming workers entered a backpressure state and terminated idle websocket sessions after a failed heartbeat reconciliation path.
mitigation_summary: Hotfixes deployed within 2 hours: reverted the prioritization change, increased streaming lane concurrency, and tuned the per-session idle timer from 180s to 300s to avoid premature disconnects. Rolling restart of the affected worker pool completed within the next 90 minutes. Temporary circuit-breaker enabled to route traffic to a smaller but stable runtime pool for premium customers.
action_items: 1) Scheduler rollback audit: add test coverage for streaming vs control request preemption and add 2 unit tests + 1 e2e test. Owner: Ethan Rivera. Status: In Progress.
2) KV-cache eviction race: instrument detailed trace spans and add a fast-path lock for active streaming sessions. Owner: Priya Shah. Status: Planned.
3) Streaming runbook update: document new thresholds, heartbeat reconciliation logic, and manual rollback steps. Owner: SRE Team (lead: Marco Li). Status: In Progress.
4) Autoscaling policy review: create a canary autoscale configuration that preserves a minimum streaming lane capacity during sudden spikes. Owner: Olivia Park. Status: Backlog.
5) Dashboard and alerts: add a derived metric for 'streaming output gap seconds' and alert at >3s sustained gap across >1% of sessions. Owner: Observability (lead: Javier Morales). Status: In Review.
6) Customer communication: collate affected customer list and prepare post-incident note. Owner: Blake Foster (CS). Status: Planned.
7) Load test: reproduce priority inversion using synthetic short-control bursts + long streaming sessions and validate fixes. Owner: Performance Eng (lead: Ada Nguyen). Status: Planned.
8) Release gating: add build-time integration tests into CI that run the synthetic priority inversion scenario on a small runtime. Owner: CI Team. Status: Backlog.
9) Long-term: evaluate admission control based on request criticality and token-rate shaping. Owner: Research/Runtime. Status: Backlog.
10) Postmortem doc & retro: finalize Confluence postmortem and run a 60-minute retro; include incident blameless timeline and decisions. Owner: Nora Kaplan. Status: In Progress.

postmortem_notes: Lesson 1: Changes to scheduler comparators require explicit e2e tests that include long-lived streaming sessions to catch priority inversion.
Lesson 2: Heartbeat and idle-timer interactions with backpressure must be validated under CPU-constrained scenarios; increase test coverage around timers.
Lesson 3: Observability gaps: we lacked a concise metric for output continuity which delayed detection. Added 'streaming output gap seconds' metric as an immediate fix.
Lesson 4: Operational mitigations (circuit-break routing) reduced blast radius for top-tier customers; formalize this as a standard escalation play.
Action: Revisit release checklist to include streaming-sensitive behavioral tests and a mandatory review for scheduler changes.
